role: original logical acceptance descriptions for the F06 geometry contract; not an engine, mesh or USD fixture
comparison: Owner amendment 2026-10-15 to CR-TOL-001: quantities use relative 1e-6; lengths and coordinates use 0.001 mm + 1e-6*abs(expected); dimensionless frame values use absolute 1e-6 at zero and relative 1e-6 otherwise. Exact rational references are unchanged. IDs, codes, statuses, counts, strings and digests compare exactly. This is test comparison only, separate from geometry decisions/certificates. The read-only first-scope package 0.1.0 retains its older rule pending review. Decimal strings are exact references unless marked approximate; JSON numbers are nearest binary64 inputs.
assumptions: P-1 replaced by contour input, P-2 confirmed unchanged and P-3 refined by the owner on 2026-10-15. The legacy assumes field identifies these decisions. Contour caps/winding/planarity and the missing angle cap are assumptions in F04 section 3. Constants are owner-confirmed first-slice draft values, to be validated by fixtures; the ifc-lite numeric comparison is recorded in docs/design/tolerance-comparison-v0.1.md.
quaternion_convention: F04 section 3: orientation_xyzw = (x, y, z, w), Hamilton, active rotation, world = R(q) * local + translation. The 90 degree turn about +Z is written with the nearest f64 0.7071067811865476 for both z and w.

cases.title: Plate mesh: counts, Euler characteristic, closed shell, outward winding
given: Valid plate 1000 x 500 x 10 mm, identity placement, element-local space; P-1 frame
cases.derivation: Vertex i = (xb, yb, zb) with i = xb + 2*yb + 4*zb sits at (1000*xb, 500*yb, 10*zb). Faces x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 are the quads [0,4,6,2], [1,3,7,5], [0,1,5,4], [2,6,7,3], [0,2,3,1], [4,5,7,6]; quad [a,b,c,d] yields triangles (a,b,c) and (a,c,d). The 12 box edges each lie in two faces and the 6 face diagonals each lie in two triangles of one face, so the triangle mesh has 12 + 6 = 18 edges: V - E + F = 8 - 18 + 12 = 2, and for the 6-face topology 8 - 12 + 6 = 2. The face normal is (b - a) x (c - a) of the first triangle of the face; its sign pattern is listed (x0: -x, x1: +x, y0: -y, y1: +y, z0: -z, z1: +z), so every face points away from the body. Signed volume = (1/6) * sum over triangles of v0 . (v1 x v2) = 5,000,000 mm3 (divergence theorem) = 1000*500*10; positive means outward.

cases.title: Plate mesh blob: byte size, layout and digest are deterministic
given: Plate 1000 x 500 x 10 mm, identity placement, element-local blob built twice from the same input
cases.derivation: Length = 32 + 24*8 + pad8(12*12) + pad8(2*12) = 32 + 192 + 144 + 24 = 392 bytes; offsets 32, 32 + 192 = 224, 224 + 144 = 368 and 368 + 24 = 392. The digest is the SHA-256 of the 392 bytes laid out by section 6 of the contract: magic BCMESH01, then little-endian u32 layout 1, vertex count 8, triangle count 12, face count 6, space 0 and reserved 0; eight vertices as little-endian binary64 with negative zero normalized; twelve u32 index triples; twelve u16 face indices. It was computed by a throwaway script from those rules.

cases.title: Plate quantities and local bounds; mass unknown without density
given: Plate 1000 x 500 x 10 mm; no material
Same plate with explicit density 1000 kg/m3

The harness binds an actual validated original profile fixture; no placeholder digest

given: Straight member with rectangular profile (explicit width and height), identity placement, element-local space
The harness binds an actual validated original profile fixture; no placeholder digest

Z_m = -0.48 + 0.48 = 0 and Y_m . (0,0,1) = 0.6 > 0. X_m = Y_m x Z_m = (-0.8*0.8 - 0.6*0.6, 0, 0) = (-1, 0, 0). The harness binds an actual validated original profile fixture; no placeholder digest

cases.title: Parallel test just inside the threshold: column rule
given: Draft policy G-06: the axis is parallel to local Z when sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) < 1e-6 * L (strict)
cases.derivation: h = 0.0005 and L = sqrt(1000^2 + 0.0005^2) ~ 1000.000000000125, so h/L ~ 5e-7 < 1e-6 with a factor-two margin: the decision does not depend on rounding. Column rule: Y_m = (0, 1, 0) exactly; Z_m is still the true axis direction (only the roll rule is switched) and X_m = Y_m x Z_m. The approximate vectors were computed in binary64 as a regression aid; only the branch and Y_m are asserted exactly.

cases.title: Parallel test just outside the threshold: horizontal rule
given: Draft policy G-06: the axis is parallel to local Z when sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) < 1e-6 * L (strict)
cases.derivation: h = 0.002, LL = 250000000001/250000 and L = sqrt(250000000001)/500 ~ 1000.0000000020000000; h/L ~ 1.9999999999960000000e-6 > 1e-6 with a factor-two margin: the horizontal rule applies. Y_m = (-dx*dz, -dy*dz, h^2)/(h*L) = (-2, 0, 4e-6)/(0.002*L) = (-1000/L, 0, 0.002/L), with Y_m . (0,0,1) = h/L > 0, and X_m = Y_m x Z_m = (0, 1, 0). For this +X tilt from +Z, the horizontal frame is exactly +90 degrees about the same axis from the near-vertical branch frame (right-hand rule). This is also the limiting roll jump between F06-POS-09 and this case as their axes approach the threshold; their finite axes differ, so their full relative rotation is not solely about one common axis (contract section 4). The exact forms use rational decimal inputs; binary64 results are compared with CR-TOL-001.

cases.title: Rotated and translated plate: world mesh, bounds and invariants
given: Plate 1000 x 500 x 10 mm; placement +90 degrees about +Z (q = (0, 0, 1/sqrt 2, 1/sqrt 2)) then translation (100, 200, 300)
cases.derivation: R(q) for +90 degrees about +Z maps (x, y, z) to (-y, x, z) (F04 worked example). World vertex = R*local + t = (100 - y, 200 + x, 300 + z). The local box [0,1000] x [0,500] x [0,10] gives x in [100 - 500, 100] = [-400, 100], y in [200, 200 + 1000] = [200, 1200] and z in [300, 310]. A proper rotation preserves orientation, so the signed volume stays 5,000,000 mm3 and the triangle tables are unchanged. The shape key excludes placement; the world key includes it.

cases.title: Rotated and translated horizontal member: world bounds
given: Member of F06-POS-04 with placement +90 degrees about +Z and translation (-50, 70, 1000)

cases.title: Member quantities: mass current with explicit density, unknown without
given: Member of F06-POS-04 (200 x 300 section, axis length 4000)
Run once without density and once with 2000 kg/m3
cases.derivation: V = 200*300*4000 = 240,000,000 mm3 = 0.24 m3; S = 2*(60,000 + 800,000 + 1,200,000) = 4,120,000 mm2 = 4.12 m2; m = 0.24*2000 = 480 kg. For this axis-aligned member the bounding box happens to have the same volume, but a bounds volume is still never reported as volume or mass.

cases.title: Minimum nonzero dimension exactly at the limit is accepted
given: Draft policy G-06: minimum nonzero dimension 0.001 mm (inclusive)
Plate 1000 x 500 x 0.001 and member axis (0,0,0) to (0.001,0,0) with section 200 x 300
cases.derivation: sqrt(x*x) equals |x| exactly in binary64 (no overflow or underflow), so an axis along one coordinate has length exactly the submitted f64 value 0.001, which equals the minimum constant, and is accepted. Plate V = 1000*500*0.001 = 500 mm3 = 5e-7 m3; member V = 200*300*0.001 = 60 mm3. The decimal 0.001 is not exactly representable; the expected values are the exact decimal products and are compared with CR-TOL-001.

cases.title: Section dimension exactly at the 1,000,000 mm cap is accepted
given: Member axis (0,0,0) to (0,0,1000) with section 1000000 x 1000000
cases.derivation: V = 10^6 * 10^6 * 10^3 = 10^15 mm3 = 10^6 m3. The cap equals the F04 plate-dimension cap (draft proposal; F04 has no section cap).

cases.title: FeatureId stability: rebuild, placement edit and dimension edit keep the same ids
given: Rebuild with identical input; then a placement-only update; then width 1000 -> 750
cases.derivation: A FeatureId is "fid1:" + ElementId + ":" + local id; the local id is built only from the body kind and the role tokens of the faces that meet at the feature (6 faces + 12 edges + 8 vertices = 26). No input of that string depends on dimensions, placement, vertex order or triangle order, so only a change of ElementId, body kind or rule version changes it. Mesh bytes are a pure function of the shape input: identical after rebuild, different after a width change.

cases.title: FeatureId uniqueness across copies: new element identity, new FeatureIds
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 and its copy 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000006 (F04 CopyElement), same shape, same local ids
cases.derivation: The qualified id embeds the 36-character ElementId, so the 26 ids of the source and the 26 of the copy are pairwise different (52 distinct strings). The shape key and the element-local mesh bytes depend only on the shape, so they are shared until an edit, as F04 requires.

cases.title: FeatureId grammar and bounded length
given: Longest form: member vertex with three role tokens
cases.derivation: "fid1:" (5) + ElementId (36) + ":" (1) + "member:" (7) + "v.x1.y1.z1" (10) = 59 bytes, below the 64-byte cap. Edge tokens name the two faces ordered by axis (x before y before z); vertex tokens name three faces in axis order; mesh vertex index i maps to the role bits (xb, yb, zb) with i = xb + 2*yb + 4*zb.

cases.title: Key values: shape key, world-measurement key and mass signature test vectors
given: Owner-amended section 7 preimages: algorithm/tolerance versions 3, feature/layout 1; ordered contour encoded, default roll zero.
cases.derivation: Computed as SHA-256 (RFC 6234) over the exact byte strings defined in section 7 by a throwaway script. The negated quaternion normalizes to the same bytes after the canonical sign rule (w >= 0), so the world key is equal; the identity and rotated placements give different world keys over the same shape key; the three mass signatures differ. These vectors fix the draft encoding: any change of it raises a version field and regenerates the vectors. Owner amendment 2026-10-15 regenerates seven digests and the antipodal equality assertion for contour encoding and versions 2/2/1/1; no analytic expected value changes. The local-size amendment regenerates these seven digests with versions 3/3/1/1 (world 3/3, mass algorithm 3); the antipodal assertion is rechecked. No preimage field, feature/layout version or baseline mesh byte changes.

cases.title: Copy shares keys: a copy of an unmodified element has the same shape key
cases.derivation: Keys hash geometry-determining inputs only and contain no ElementId, so a copy shares them and the cached geometry. FeatureIds contain the ElementId and so differ (F06-POS-17).

cases.title: Mesh blob header exactly at the caps is accepted by structural validation
given: Header-only structural validation of a blob declaring 4096 vertices, 8192 triangles and 1024 faces; no allocation before the checks
cases.derivation: 32 + 24*4096 + pad8(12*8192) + pad8(2*8192) = 32 + 98,304 + 98,304 + 16,384 = 213,024 bytes. All three counts equal their caps and are accepted; this checks length and counts only, not topology.

cases.title: Snapshot chunking: twenty bodies in whole-blob pages under the F05 attachment limit
given: Twenty plate bodies (392-byte blobs each); negotiated attachments per bundle and buffer size at the F05 maxima
cases.derivation: F05 allows at most 8 attachments per bundle (F05 sections 3 and 10) and each blob (392 bytes, at most 213,024) is far below the per-attachment cap. Whole blobs only: ceil(20 / 8) = 3 pages holding 8, 8 and 4 blobs. If a smaller attachment limit is negotiated, the page count follows from the same rule.

cases.title: Ray pick: front face hit, back faces culled by default
cases.derivation: The ray enters the box through the top face z = 10 at t = 100 - 10 = 90, point (500, 250, 10), outward normal +Z; direction . normal = -1 < 0, so the face is front-facing. The bottom face z = 0 is crossed at t = 100 with outward normal (0, 0, -1); direction . normal = +1 > 0, so it is back-facing and culled by default. The omitted t_max_mm defaults to 4,000,000,000 mm; both face intersections are within the finite parameter interval.

cases.title: Ray pick with back faces included: both hits, ascending t
given: Same plate and ray as F06-POS-29, include_backfaces = true
cases.derivation: Top face at t = 90 (front-facing); bottom face at t = 100 with outward normal (0, 0, -1) equal to the ray direction, so direction . normal = +1 > 0 (back-facing). Ascending t gives the order. Both parameters lie in the default finite interval [0, 4,000,000,000] mm.

cases.title: Pick tie-break: equal distance orders by ElementId
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 and its copy 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000006 with identical placement, so both top faces are hit at the same t
cases.derivation: Both hit at t = 90, so the quantized distance keys are equal (floor(90 / 0.001) twice). The next key is the canonical ElementId string; ...0005 sorts before ...0006. Both hits are within the default finite interval [0, 4,000,000,000] mm.

cases.title: Pick tie-break: equal distance orders by FeatureId string, edge picks
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 1000 x 500 x 10, ray along an edge, targets edge, radius 0
cases.derivation: The ray runs along x = 0, z = 10. Edge x0.z1 (x = 0, z = 10, y in [0, 500]) overlaps it: distance 0, and for an overlap the smallest t attaining the minimum is 100 (point (0, 0, 10)). Edges x0.y0 (x = 0, y = 0) and y0.z1 (y = 0, z = 10) cross it at (0, 0, 10), t = 100. Edges x0.y1 and y1.z1 cross it at (0, 500, 10), t = 600. Every other edge is at distance >= 10. At t = 100 the three FeatureIds are ordered by ASCII comparison of the local part ("e.x0.y0" < "e.x0.z1" < "e.y0.z1"); at t = 600 likewise ("e.x0.y1" < "e.y1.z1"). These are distances to the closed finite pick segment with default t_max_mm = 4,000,000,000, not to an unbounded ray; the zero-distance overlap is t in [100, 600], whose smallest parameter is 100. All reported parameters are inside that interval.

cases.title: Point pick within a radius
cases.derivation: The distance to the plane z = 10 is 2 and the foot (500, 250, 10) lies inside the face rectangle. The bottom face is 12 away; every edge and vertex is farther than 5 (the nearest edge, y0.z1, is sqrt(250^2 + 2^2) away). This is point form: distances are to closed features and no t_max_mm or ray parameter applies.

cases.title: Incremental update after a placement-only edit: no mesh resend
given: Snapshot S0 taken at generation g; plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 then receives a placement update (generation g+1)
cases.derivation: The element-local mesh depends on the shape key only; the key is unchanged, so the consumer keeps its mesh buffer and receives the new world measurements and key.

cases.title: Incremental update after a dimension edit: mesh resent
cases.derivation: The shape key changed, so the element-local blob changes and is delivered whole.

cases.title: Incremental update with an expired token requests a full snapshot
given: Token older than the retained history
cases.derivation: The engine retains a bounded history; a token it cannot answer incrementally gets the F05 invalidation semantics (no partial list) and the consumer must read a fresh snapshot.

cases.title: Cancellation after the seal point is a no-op
given: Cancel requested after the result was sealed
cases.derivation: The seal point lies after the last cancellation point. The result is complete and identical to an uncancelled run (same digest as F06-POS-02).

cases.title: Quantity becomes stale when its shape key no longer matches
given: Volume is current for plate 1000 x 500 x 10; a width update to 750 is accepted but the rebuild has not completed
cases.derivation: F04 section 5: stale may keep a clearly marked previous value; after the rebuild the value 750*500*10 = 3,750,000 mm3 = 0.00375 m3 is current again.

cases.title: Headless parity: engine API and CLI return the same logical result
given: Same revision and element, once through the engine API and once through the CLI mesh query
cases.derivation: AGENTS.md section 3: every feature has an engine API first and a CLI command; the CLI adds no computation (contract section 9).

cases.title: Element list order is canonical
given: Elements created in the order ...0006 then ...0005

expected.order_rule: ascending ElementId, ASCII comparison of the canonical lowercase string

cases.derivation: Result order never depends on creation order, hash-map order or triangle order, so pages and cursors are reproducible.

cases.title: Non-finite plate dimension
given: Typed input from an API client (not JSON text): NaN width
cases.derivation: Every f64 is checked for finiteness before any range check. JSON NaN/Infinity literals never reach the kernel (F04-RAW-01, F04-RAW-02).

cases.title: Non-finite placement component
given: Translation component -Infinity, valid body
cases.derivation: The finiteness stage covers body, axis points, profile, translation and quaternion, in input order.

cases.title: Plate dimension below the minimum nonzero dimension
given: Draft policy G-06: 0 < d < 0.001 mm is rejected
cases.derivation: 0.0009 > 0 passes the F04 range but is below 0.001 mm; zero itself is GEO_NOT_POSITIVE (F04-NEG-04).

cases.title: Member axis shorter than the minimum
cases.derivation: Length 0.0009 < 0.001. Exactly zero length uses the same diagnostic (F04-NEG-20, adopted G-03).

cases.title: Degenerate (zero-length) axis at the kernel
given: Identical axis points
cases.derivation: Length exactly 0 is below the minimum; no direction can be formed, so no frame is attempted and no division by zero occurs.

cases.title: Section dimension above the cap
given: Section width 1000000.001 mm
cases.derivation: Draft proposal: the section cap equals the F04 plate-dimension cap 1,000,000 mm; F04 itself is silent on section dimensions.

cases.title: Section dimension zero
given: Section height 0
cases.derivation: A zero section dimension produces no solid.

cases.title: Curved profile is unsupported
given: Profile kind "circle" with a diameter
cases.derivation: The first scope supports only the rectangle section; a well-formed shape outside the scope is UNSUPPORTED_GEOMETRY, not INVALID_ARGUMENT.

cases.title: Scaled or sheared transform is unsupported
given: Placement offered as a 3x3 matrix with scale 2
cases.derivation: Only a rigid pose (translation and unit quaternion) is accepted; scale, shear and reflection are unsupported in the first scope (F04 section 3).

cases.title: Imported mesh stage frame is unsupported
given: Mesh source declaring metersPerUnit = 0.01 and upAxis = Y
cases.derivation: Unit and axis conversion for imported meshes belongs to later R-tasks; until then the kernel does not guess.

cases.title: Vertex count above the cap
given: Blob header declaring 4097 vertices
cases.derivation: One above the 4096-vertex cap (F06-POS-27); rejected from the header, before any size computation or allocation.

cases.title: Triangle count above the cap
given: Blob header declaring 8193 triangles
cases.derivation: One above the 8192-triangle cap.

cases.title: Face count above the cap
given: Blob header declaring 1025 faces
cases.derivation: One above the 1024-face cap.

cases.title: Header counts that overflow a 32-bit size computation
given: All three counts 4294967295
cases.derivation: Counts are compared with their caps before any multiplication; the products would exceed 2^32 but are never computed in a narrow type (checked 64-bit arithmetic).

cases.title: Blob length disagrees with the header
given: Header of F06-POS-02 (392 bytes) but only 391 bytes supplied
cases.derivation: The computed length is 392; any mismatch, nonzero reserved field, bad magic, unknown layout version, non-finite coordinate or out-of-range index is GEO_BLOB_INVALID.

cases.title: Cancelled before the build
given: Cancellation observed at the first cancellation point (after validation)
cases.derivation: No mesh, no quantities and no shape key are returned as current; the diagnostic names the stage "build".

cases.title: Cancelled before the quantities
given: Cancellation observed at the point before quantity evaluation
cases.derivation: A built but unsealed mesh is discarded; cancellation never returns a result that has a mesh but no quantities as current.

cases.title: Open mesh never receives exact status
given: A blob equal to the plate mesh with its ninth triangle (0, 2, 3), the first triangle of face z0, removed (11 triangles)
cases.derivation: Removing triangle (0, 2, 3) leaves the edges 0-2, 2-3 and 3-0 each used by one triangle only (boundary edges), so edge-triangle incidence is not 2 everywhere. The edge count stays 18 and F = 11, so V - E + F = 8 - 18 + 11 = 1. The signed-volume sum of the remaining triangles is not a volume. No exact status and no value. Mass is unsupported, not unknown, because the volume is unsupported (contract section 8 precedence); a density could not make it current.

cases.title: Closed but self-intersecting mesh never receives exact status
given: Two closed 10 x 10 x 10 mm boxes overlapping for x in [5, 10], supplied as one blob (16 vertices, 24 triangles)
cases.derivation: Each box is closed (every edge in two triangles, opposite directions) and the signed sum is 1000 + 1000 = 2000 mm3, but the true union volume is 1500 mm3 (the overlap 5*10*10 = 500 is counted twice). Nothing in the first scope certifies a mesh free of self-intersection, so a mesh not produced by the analytic builder gets no exact status; the wrong number 2000 is never reported. V - E + F = 16 - 36 + 24 = 4 = 2 * 2 for two shells.

cases.title: Inward winding is rejected as an outward mesh
given: The plate mesh with every triangle reversed
cases.derivation: Reversing every triangle keeps all edge pairs opposite (still closed) and flips the sign of the divergence-theorem sum to -5,000,000 mm3: the normals point into the body. The contract accepts only outward meshes, so no quantity is derived from it.

cases.title: Failure never replaces the current geometry
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 has a current mesh and volume 0.005 m3; an update to thickness 0.0009 is requested
cases.derivation: A failed result carries no geometry, and the engine neither replaces nor stales the previous current result because of a rejected command (F04 section 8: rejection leaves derived state unchanged).

cases.title: Unknown FeatureId
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005; well-formed id for the other body kind: a member face
cases.derivation: The id is syntactically valid but names no feature of this element (a plate has no "member" features).

cases.title: Malformed FeatureId
given: Uppercase hexadecimal in the element identity
cases.derivation: The grammar requires the canonical lowercase UUIDv7 form (F04 section 2) and the version tag fid1.

cases.title: A triangle index cannot address a feature
given: Lookup request carrying a triangle_index field
cases.derivation: Query and reference schemas are closed; there is no triangle-index field. Drawings and dimensions address features by FeatureId only.

cases.title: Stale snapshot token on a read query
given: Query pinned to a token from an older generation than the retained history
cases.derivation: A query answered at one revision is never mixed with data from another; the consumer re-reads.

cases.title: Pick with a zero ray direction
given: direction (0, 0, 0)
cases.derivation: The direction norm must be at least 1e-9; a zero vector cannot be normalized.

cases.title: Pick with a non-finite origin
given: origin x = NaN
cases.derivation: Same finiteness rule as the kernel input.

cases.title: Pick requests more hits than the cap
given: max_hits 65 with cap 64
cases.derivation: One above the 64-hit cap; max_hits = 64 is accepted.

cases.title: Pick radius above the cap
given: radius_mm 1000000.001
cases.derivation: One thousandth above the 1,000,000 mm radius cap.

cases.title: Empty mesh
given: Header with zero vertices and zero triangles
cases.derivation: A body has at least four vertices and four triangles; zero counts are structurally invalid, never an "empty success".

cases.title: Near-vertical axis tilted toward +Y: section stays perpendicular to the axis
given: Draft policy G-06: near-vertical rule when hh < 1e-12 * LL; Y = normalize(U - Z*(U . Z)), U = (0, 1, 0)
cases.derivation: d = (0, 0.08000002, 160000.08); with m = 4,000,001 the three numbers are 2m, m^2 - 1 and m^2 + 1 times 1e-8, so L = (m^2 + 1) * 1e-8 = 160000.08000002 exactly (a^2 + c^2 = L^2 checked with rational arithmetic) and hh/LL = (2m/(m^2 + 1))^2 ~ 2.4999987500001562502e-13 < 1e-12, so the near-vertical rule applies (margin 4). Z = (0, 2m/(m^2 + 1), (m^2 - 1)/(m^2 + 1)). U . Z = Z_y; P = U - Z*Z_y = (0, 1 - Z_y^2, -Z_z*Z_y) = Z_z * (0, Z_z, -Z_y) because 1 - Z_y^2 = Z_z^2; |P| = Z_z, so Y = (0, Z_z, -Z_y) (unit). X0 = Y x Z = (Z_z^2 + Z_y^2, 0, 0) = (1, 0, 0), so X = (1, 0, 0) and Z x X = (0, Z_z, -Z_y) = Y. Y . Z = Z_z*Z_y - Z_y*Z_z = 0. A fixed Y = (0, 1, 0) would give Y . Z = Z_y ~ 5e-7, i.e. a section off perpendicular by the tilt toward Y. The submitted decimals are not exact in binary64, so the frame is compared with CR-TOL-001.

cases.title: Boundary: Y-tilted axis just outside the threshold uses the horizontal rule
given: hh/LL = (0.002/L)^2 ~ 4e-12 > 1e-12, a factor-four margin
cases.derivation: h = 0.002, LL = 250000000001/250000 and L = sqrt(250000000001)/500 ~ 1000.0000000020000000; hh/LL = 1/250000000001 ~ 3.9999999999840000000e-12 > 1e-12. Y_m = (-dx*dz, -dy*dz, hh)/(h*L) = (0, -2, 4e-6)/(0.002*L) = (0, -1000/L, 0.002/L), Z_m = (0, 0.002/L, 1000/L) and X_m = Y_m x Z_m = (-1, 0, 0). For this +Y tilt from +Z, the horizontal frame is exactly 180 degrees about the same axis from the near-vertical branch frame: both X and Y reverse. F06-POS-41 uses the near-vertical rule on a different +Y-tilted axis; as the two axes approach the threshold, the limiting roll jump is a half turn (contract section 4, rule 3). At their finite tilts the axes also differ. The exact forms use rational decimal inputs; binary64 results are compared with CR-TOL-001.

cases.title: Ray pick on a face boundary: reported once, flagged, parallel neighbour skipped
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 1000 x 500 x 10, identity placement; the ray hits the shared edge of faces z1 and x0
cases.derivation: The ray runs along x = 0, z falling; it meets the plane z = 10 at t = 90, point (0, 250, 10), on the boundary x = 0 of the rectangle of z1, so boundary is true. Face x0 (plane x = 0) has outward normal (-1, 0, 0) and u . n = 0 < 1e-6: parallel, not hit. Face z0 is back-facing and culled. Exactly one hit. The hit t = 90 is within the default finite interval [0, 4,000,000,000] mm; the pick band does not extend that interval for faces.

cases.title: Ray pick parallel to faces: parallel faces are never hit, boundary hit flagged
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005; ray in the plane z = 10 travelling along +X from outside
cases.derivation: Faces z1, z0, y0 and y1 have normals perpendicular to the direction (1, 0, 0), so |u . n| = 0 < 1e-6 and they are parallel: no hit, even though the ray lies in the plane of z1. Face x0 has normal (-1, 0, 0), u . n = -1 (front-facing), t = 10, point (0, 250, 10): z = 10 is the upper boundary of x0, so boundary is true. Face x1 at t = 1010 is back-facing and culled. Both face parameters lie in the default finite interval [0, 4,000,000,000] mm; the pick band does not extend that interval for faces.

cases.title: Point pick: distance to the nearest point of a closed face rectangle, ordering by quantized distance
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 1000 x 500 x 10; point (1100, 250, 5) lies outside the box, beyond face x1
cases.derivation: Face x1 (x = 1000, y in [0, 500], z in [0, 10]): the foot (1000, 250, 5) is inside, distance 100. Faces z0 and z1: the foot (1100, 250, 0 or 10) lies outside the rectangle (x > 1000), so the distance is to the nearest rectangle point (1000, 250, 0 or 10): sqrt(100^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(10025) ~ 100.12492197250392864. Edges x1.z0 and x1.z1 have the same nearest points and distance. Every other face, edge and vertex is at least sqrt(100^2 + 250^2) = sqrt(72500) ~ 269.25824035672520156 away (a brute-force check over all 26 features agrees). Order by the tuple (floor(distance / 0.001), ElementId, kind rank, local id): x1 first (smaller distance), then the four features at sqrt(10025), faces before edges, "plate:f.z0" < "plate:f.z1", "plate:e.x1.z0" < "plate:e.x1.z1". This is point form; the finite ray horizon does not apply and these expected distances are unchanged.

cases.title: Parallel decision very close to the threshold follows the written binary64 comparison
given: Axis (0,0,0) to (0.5, 0, 500000): hh = 0.25 and LL = 250000000000.25, both exactly representable
cases.derivation: Exact arithmetic: 0.25 < 1e-12 * 250000000000.25 = 0.25000000000025, margin 1e-12 relative, which is thousands of ulps, so the written binary64 comparison agrees with exact arithmetic here and selects the near-vertical rule. The contract does not rely on that agreement in general: the written comparison decides, and either branch gives a certified frame. Z_y = 0 gives Y = (0, 1, 0) exactly. L ~ 500000.00000025 is below the 1,000,000 mm cap.

cases.title: Frame certificate failure is reported as numeric uncertainty, no partial result
given: Valid member; the test harness injects a fault so that the built frame has X . Y = 2e-6 (above the 1e-6 certificate limit)
cases.derivation: The frame certificate (section 4, rule 2, step e) requires the absolute value of every pairwise dot product to be at most 1e-6; |+2e-6| = 2e-6 fails it. The build stops, no mesh, quantities or shape key is returned, the previous current result is untouched. This case needs a fault-injection hook in the harness; it is not reachable from admitted input.

cases.title: Pick result with a failed numeric certificate returns no partial hits
given: Valid pick; the test harness injects a non-finite intermediate value into the face-hit computation
cases.derivation: A query whose certificate fails returns the diagnostic and no hits, never a list that omits the affected candidate.

cases.title: Pick over more elements than the work cap
given: A model with 65,537 elements (the cap is 65,536; exactly 65,536 is accepted)
cases.derivation: The element count is compared with the cap before the scan starts; one above is rejected without work and without hits.

cases.title: Negotiated buffer limit smaller than the blob: no splitting
given: F05 effective_limits.buffer_bytes negotiated as 391; the plate blob of F06-POS-02 is 392 bytes
cases.derivation: A blob is one attachment and is never fragmented; 392 > 391 fails, 392 <= 392 fits. The contract cap (213,024) is a maximum, the negotiated limit applies when smaller.

cases.title: Frame certificate: a negative pairwise dot product beyond the limit fails (absolute value)
given: Valid member; the harness injects the frame X = (1, 0, 0), Y = (-2e-6, 1, 0), Z = (0, 0, 1), so X . Y = -2e-6
cases.derivation: Exact arithmetic: |X|^2 = 1 and |Z|^2 = 1; |Y|^2 - 1 = 4e-12, within 1e-6; (X x Y) . Z = 1 - 0 = 1, so the norm and handedness checks pass. X . Y = -2e-6 and |X . Y| = 2e-6 > 1e-6, so the certificate fails. A bound written without the absolute value (X . Y <= 1e-6) would accept this frame, which is why step e requires |X . Y|, |X . Z| and |Y . Z| each at most 1e-6. With F06-NEG-31 (+2e-6) the pair exercises both signs of an injected error. Fault injection is a harness hook; the frame is not reachable from admitted input.

cases.title: Finite ray: edges and vertex at the horizon endpoint are accepted
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 1000 x 500 x 10, identity placement; vertex v.x0.y0.z1 is (0, 0, 10); the ray starts at (0, -100, 10) along +Y
cases.derivation: Exact arithmetic: (v - o) . u = 100; t_max_mm = 100, so the closest segment point is its endpoint (0, 0, 10), distance 0. The three closed edges x0.y0, x0.z1 and y0.z1 share that point and also have distance 0 with smallest minimizing t = 100. Every other edge or vertex is at least 10 mm away. All four hits have floor(t / 1e-6) = 100000000; edge rank precedes vertex rank and the three edge local ids sort x0.y0, x0.z1, y0.z1. The inclusive endpoint band accepts distance 0 with radius 0.

cases.title: Finite ray: reject edges and vertices reached only beyond a short horizon
given: Plate 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000-000000000005 1000 x 500 x 10, identity placement; vertex v.x0.y0.z1 is (0, 0, 10); the ray starts at (0, -100, 10) along +Y
cases.derivation: Exact arithmetic: the unbounded ray reaches vertex (0, 0, 10) at t = 100 with distance 0. Clamping to [0, 50] gives t = 50, segment endpoint (0, -50, 10), squared distance 2500 mm2 and distance 50 mm. The same three incident edges as F06-POS-47 have this minimum; all other edges and vertices are at least 50 mm away because every feature has y >= 0 while the segment has y <= -50. Thus every edge/vertex distance exceeds radius_mm + eps_pick = 0.000001 mm and there are no hits. This is a successful empty query, not invalid input; extending the ray would incorrectly return hits.

cases.title: Rectangle first edge along element-local +Y
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: Exact vectors p1-p0 and p3-p0 have lengths 1000 and 500, cross product +Z. V=1000*500*10/10^9=0.005; S=2*(1000*500+1000*10+500*10)/10^6=1.03. Add (0,0,10) for top vertices; coordinate extrema give the listed bounds. Counts remain 8,12,26.

cases.title: Rectangle starts at opposite corner
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: Exact vectors p1-p0 and p3-p0 have lengths 1000 and 500, cross product +Z. V=1000*500*10/10^9=0.005; S=2*(1000*500+1000*10+500*10)/10^6=1.03. Add (0,0,10) for top vertices; coordinate extrema give the listed bounds. Counts remain 8,12,26.

given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: F04 section 3 ordered contour validity checks reject this input before the rectangle support decision; no authored state or partial geometry changes.

given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.

given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.

given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.

cases.title: Repeated consecutive contour points rejected
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: F04 section 3 ordered contour validity checks reject this input before the rectangle support decision; no authored state or partial geometry changes.

cases.title: Valid pentagon is unsupported, not invalid
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: Contour validity succeeds. Five points cannot meet the exactly-four-point rectangle support rule. No shape key or quantities are returned; model input remains valid.

cases.title: Explicit zero roll equals omitted roll
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: Ideal angle reference: 0 or pi/2 is supplied as nearest f64. At zero X/Y are unchanged; at pi/2 X_r=Y_0 and Y_r=-X_0, Z unchanged. For the near-vertical Pythagorean axis use A=8000004000000, B=4000001, C=8000004000001, with A^2+B^2=C^2. The default frame has X_0=(1,0,0), Y_0=(0,A/C,-B/C), Z=(0,B/C,A/C). These exact references use CR-TOL-001, not an assertion that f64 pi/2 has exact cosine zero.

cases.title: Positive pi/2 roll about member local +Z
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: Ideal angle reference: 0 or pi/2 is supplied as nearest f64. At zero X/Y are unchanged; at pi/2 X_r=Y_0 and Y_r=-X_0, Z unchanged. For the near-vertical Pythagorean axis use A=8000004000000, B=4000001, C=8000004000001, with A^2+B^2=C^2. The default frame has X_0=(1,0,0), Y_0=(0,A/C,-B/C), Z=(0,B/C,A/C). These exact references use CR-TOL-001, not an assertion that f64 pi/2 has exact cosine zero.

cases.title: Roll after the near-vertical default frame
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: Ideal angle reference: 0 or pi/2 is supplied as nearest f64. At zero X/Y are unchanged; at pi/2 X_r=Y_0 and Y_r=-X_0, Z unchanged. For the near-vertical Pythagorean axis use A=8000004000000, B=4000001, C=8000004000001, with A^2+B^2=C^2. The default frame has X_0=(1,0,0), Y_0=(0,A/C,-B/C), Z=(0,B/C,A/C). These exact references use CR-TOL-001, not an assertion that f64 pi/2 has exact cosine zero.

cases.title: Non-finite roll rejected
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: NaN here denotes an in-memory f64 NaN, not a JSON numeric string; kernel finiteness fails. Wire overflow is F04-RAW-07.

cases.title: Roll above assumed inclusive angle cap
given: Owner decisions of 2026-10-15; F04 section 3.
cases.derivation: 7 > 6.283185307179586 radians; the cap is an explicit assumption because no earlier cap exists.

cases.title: Large plate thickness just above the scaled floor
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: The contour sides are 3*131072 and 4*131072, so D=5*131072=655360 exactly. D/4194304=5/32=0.15625 mm; thickness=161/1024 exceeds it by 1/1024. The element-local x origin and world y translation do not enter D. Both policies accept.

cases.title: Large plate thickness exactly at the scaled floor
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: The same exact 3-4-5 contour gives D=655360 and eps_geom=5/32. Thickness=5/32 is accepted by the inclusive minimum. No input is snapped or moved.

cases.title: Small body retains the absolute floor at a large placement
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: D=sqrt(3*3+4*4)=5 exactly; 5/4194304 < binary64(0.001), so eps_geom is the binary64 0.001 constant. Thickness uses that same literal and is accepted. Repeat with identity placement: the floor and admission are identical.

cases.title: Large near-planar plate admitted under the scaled planarity band
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: Offsets (0,0,0),(a,0,s),(a,b,0),(0,b,s), a=393216, b=524288, s=3/4, give exact N=(0,0,2*a*b); the p0 plane is z=0. D=655360 exactly. Binary64 eps_plane rounds eps_geom+binary64(1e-6)*D: 0.75 is above the old 0.001+1e-6*D band and below the new band. The projected contour is a simple positive rectangle, but the authored 3D contour is not exactly planar: model input is valid, evaluation unsupported, no partial geometry or key.

cases.title: Member section half-diagonal sets the scaled floor
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: Half dimensions 196608 and 262144 form a 3-4-5 triple with H=327680. H exceeds ell=81/1024; eps_geom=H/4194304=5/64. Axis length exceeds it by 1/1024 and section dimensions exceed it. Both policies accept.

cases.title: Member axis sets the floor for a section dimension
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: ell=524288=2^19; H is below ell because (129/2048)^2+150^2 < ell^2. L=ell and eps_geom=1/8; width=129/1024 is 1/1024 above it. This checks that the member-axis scale also governs section dimensions.

cases.title: Large plate thickness just below the scaled floor
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: D=655360 and eps_geom=5/32 as in F06-POS-53. Thickness=159/1024 is 1/1024 below eps_geom but above 0.001 mm. The previous fixed floor accepted this large-coordinate plate; the scaled minimum rejects it without state change.

cases.title: Contour local size exceeds the D cap before unsupported evaluation
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: Every contour edge is either 750000 or 1000 mm, within the edge cap. D^2=2250000^2+1000^2=5062501000000 exceeds 2000000^2. All submitted coordinates are within 1e9. The D cap alone fails before the floor or polygon support decision.

cases.title: Member axis coincident under the section-scaled floor
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: The section gives H=327680 and eps_geom=5/64. ell=79/1024 is 1/1024 below the floor, although it exceeds 0.001 mm. The endpoints are coincident under the strict scaled rule; reject before normalizing the axis.

cases.title: Member section dimension below the axis-scaled floor
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: ell=524288; H is below ell because (127/2048)^2+150^2 < ell^2. L=ell, eps_geom=1/8 and width=127/1024 is 1/1024 below it. The old 0.001 mm minimum accepted this width; the scaled rule rejects it.

cases.title: Large contour outside the scaled planarity band
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: The same saddle contour as F06-POS-56 with s=7/8 has N=(0,0,2*a*b) and D=655360. Its maximum distance 7/8 exceeds binary64(eps_geom + binary64(1e-6)*D), so contour admission fails before rectangle support.

cases.title: Member local size above the axis cap is never clamped
given: Owner local-size decision 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 section 4.
cases.derivation: ell=1000000.5 exceeds H and the 1000000 mm axis/L cap. The scale is rejected before epsilon calculation; the cap is not widened.

cases.title: Non-finite derived local size never falls back to 0.001 mm
given: Finite capped small plate; harness injects an arithmetic fault after local-size derivation.
cases.derivation: Non-finite derived L cannot enter max or key encoding. This fault is unreachable from finite inputs under the stated caps; the harness tests failure handling, not a valid model.

cases.title: Scaled body floor does not widen the absolute pick boundary band
given: Valid large plate of F06-POS-53; one element; point-form vertex pick, radius zero.
cases.derivation: The point is 1/128 mm outside vertex p0 along -X, an exactly representable difference at this origin. 0.001 < 1/128 < 5/32=eps_geom. All other vertices are farther away. Section 9 still uses eps_pick=0.001 mm, so no vertex qualifies; eps_geom is not a pick band.

cases.title: Large negative section width is not positive, never above-limit
given: Review fix 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 sections 2 and 4. Valid 1000 mm axis, height 300 mm.
cases.derivation: The width passes the upper cap by value. It contributes 0 to H, so L=max(1000,150)=1000 and the call does not become an above-limit result; the range stage reports the nonpositive width.

cases.title: Huge negative section width does not overflow the scale derivation
given: Review fix 2026-10-15; F04 section 3, F06 sections 2 and 4. Valid 1000 mm axis, height 300 mm.
cases.derivation: hw would overflow if squared. A nonpositive width contributes 0 to H, so no overflow occurs and the range stage reports GEO_NOT_POSITIVE, not GEO_NUMERIC_UNCERTAIN.
